title: Hosted API: fast-fail routing shim and coordinated retry-dampener for customer escalations
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported recurring 5xx waves and timeouts during peak tenant bursts. Investigation shows harmful interaction between client SDK retries, edge proxy fanout, and backend connection admission that produced connection pool exhaustion and cascading KV-cache evictions. This ticket implements a coordinated mitigation: an edge fast-fail routing shim (low-cost path for prioritized tenants), a per-tenant retry-dampener header that instructs SDKs/edge to suppress client-side immediate retries, and a short-term server-side adaptive admission control to preserve latency SLOs while we ship a more complete fix.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create synthetic tenant load that opens 200 concurrent streaming connections with moderate per-req fanout (2-3 backend calls).
2) Configure client SDK with default exponential retry (3 attempts) and no jitter to emulate customer integration.
3) Run sustained burst for 10 minutes, gradually increase buffer of queued requests until edge begins rejecting new upstream connections.
4) Observe proxy logs for connection wait times, backend connection pool saturation, KV cache eviction rate, and spike in 5xx responses/timeouts.
investigation_findings: Edge proxy keeps per-origin connection pool; when pool saturates, requests queue and client SDK retries amplify the queue (retry amplification).
Backend microservices (runtime workers) hit socket accept stalls under extreme transient load causing timeouts and 502/504 responses to bubble up to customers.
KV cache eviction frequency increases sharply when many short-lived requests populate unique prefixes, increasing backend CPU and triggering GC pauses on some runtimes.
Current tenant-prioritization logic was insufficiently aggressive for identified enterprise customers; they observed larger error windows and higher SLA impact.
Telemetry gap: requests that were retried immediately by the SDK are not currently tagged in the same trace, making root-cause correlation difficult.
proposed_solution:
Short-term mitigation (this ticket):
    - Implement 'retry-dampener' header (x-rw-retry-dampener: level) produced by the control plane during escalations. Edge will treat this as a strong hint to suppress client-initiated immediate retries for the given tenant for a short window.

- Add a fast-fail routing shim in front of the hosted edge that detects backlog thresholds per-tenant and routes to a low-cost fastpath (priority-preserve) which returns quick degraded but successful responses or controlled 429/503 with Retry-After, avoiding cascaded 5xx.

- Apply adaptive admission control on runtime pools: when queue length crosses threshold, reduce batch size and shed non-critical requests (embeddings preprocess, low-priority jobs) rather than blocking all requests.
Medium-term actions: SDK release with tracing-preserving retry logic, better idempotency token propagation, and jitter defaults; enhanced KV cache prefix coalescing heuristics to reduce churn.
Long-term: Instrumented automatic retry-coalescer inside the edge that dedups simultaneous retries and provides consistent backpressure signals to clients.
rollout_plan: 1) Create feature-flagged implementation behind edge/hosted feature flag 'retry-dampener-v1' and 'fastpath-shim'.
2) Internal canary: enable for 5% of traffic (non-production tenants) and run for 24 hours while monitoring errors/latency/eviction metrics.
3) Customer canary: enable for 2 impacted customers (with opt-in via support) and run continuous monitoring for 72 hours.
4) Ramp to 25% traffic if metrics stable, then to 100% in 48h increments.
Rollback criteria: >10% increase in 5xx for canary tenants compared to baseline, or any increase in P99 tail latency >25ms sustained over 15m.
monitoring_and_metrics: Primary signals: per-tenant 5xx rate, per-tenant timeout rate, edge connection pool saturation, backend accept latency, KV cache eviction/sec, per-request retry count (new header-tagged metric).
Service-Level Objectives to watch: run.P50 latency, run.P99 latency, per-tenant error budget burn rate, tenant-specific SLA breaches.
Dashboards: hosted-edge/retry-dampener, runtime/pool-admission, kvcache/evictions, sdk/retry-count -- links in comments.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation behind feature flag and deployed to edge + runtime clusters.
Internal canary shows >=40% reduction in total retried requests contributing to queue length within 24h compared to pre-flag baseline.
No regression in P99 latency beyond rollback thresholds during canary.
SRE/observability tests added: synthetic consumer that verifies header propagation through edge -> runtime -> backend traces; unit + e2e tests for header handling.
